title: polyjose conformance vector
description: One file under conformance/vectors/ holds exactly one vector. Every platform runner (Rust, WASM, Node, Kotlin, Swift) must reject a file that does not match this schema, and must fail (never skip) a vector whose operation it does not implement. A vector may list in "features" the polyjose cargo features it needs; a runner where one is not enabled reports the vector SKIPPED with the feature names, and never counts it as passing. Operations without an input/expect definition here are reserved for the features that will define them; until then no runner implements them, so a vector using one fails. Bytes under test of the codec operations (b64url.*, jwk.thumbprint) are given in lowercase hex, never base64url, so the codec is not checked against itself. The jws.* and jwe.* operations give octets as canonical base64url (members ending in _b64u), the form JOSE fields natively have; the codec is not under test there.

source.description: Where the expected value comes from: an RFC section ("RFC 7638 §3.1"), an upstream suite, or "polyjose" for a project-defined negative vector.

description.description: What the vector checks, in one sentence.

features.description: Optional. The polyjose cargo features the vector needs: insecure-test-vectors for jwe.encrypt with rng_b64u or protected_b64u (ADR 0041 §3), deflate for zip (ADR 0017). A runner whose build lacks one reports the vector SKIPPED, naming the features, and never counts it as passing. The bindings never enable insecure-test-vectors (ADR 0005), so such vectors are Rust-only.

hex.description: Lowercase hexadecimal, two digits per octet; empty for zero octets.

base64url.description: Characters of the base64url alphabet (RFC 4648 §5), no padding.

count.description: A non-negative integer that an unsigned 32-bit integer holds (ADR 0030 u32), so every binding reads it natively and exactly.

jwe.description: A JWE: a string in the Compact Serialization (RFC 7516 §7.1), or an object in the flattened or general JWE JSON Serialization (RFC 7516 §7.2), which a runner passes to the library as its JSON text. Otherwise unconstrained: malformed JWEs are under test.

jws.description: A JWS: a string in the Compact Serialization (RFC 7515 §7.1), or an object in the flattened or general JWS JSON Serialization (RFC 7515 §7.2), which a runner passes to the library as its JSON text. Otherwise unconstrained: malformed JWSs are under test.

alg_list.description: An algorithm allow-list (RFC 8725 §3.1) of names, passed to the library as given: JWS "alg" names for jws.*, JWE "alg" or "enc" names for jwe.*. For jws.*, an empty list, "none" or an unknown name is refused by the library with AlgorithmNotAllowed; for jwe.*, an empty list is AlgorithmNotAllowed, and an unknown or unimplemented name may be listed but never decrypts (UnsupportedAlgorithm, the support check comes first). Vectors may test all of these.

failure.description: The operation must fail with exactly this error code.

b64url_encode_input.description: Octets to encode as unpadded base64url (RFC 7515 §2).

b64url_encode_ok.description: Encoding cannot fail, so only a success expectation exists.

b64url_decode_input.description: Text to decode; any string, since rejected encodings are under test.

jwk_thumbprint_input.description: A JWK (RFC 7517 §4) as a JSON object, imported and then hashed (RFC 7638 §3). Its members are deliberately unconstrained: invalid keys are under test.

jwk_thumbprint_ok.description: The base64url JWK Thumbprint (RFC 7638 §3) and its JWK Thumbprint URI (RFC 9278 §3).

jws_signer.description: One signature to compute: its JWS Protected Header as exact octets (RFC 7515 §5.1 step 3; the runner signs over them verbatim), its JWS Unprotected Header (RFC 7515 §7.2.1), and its key. The runner imports key, then parses protected_b64u, then header; the first error is the outcome.

protected_b64u.description: BASE64URL(UTF8(JWS Protected Header)), kept verbatim for the signing input (e.g. RFC 7515 A.1's CRLF header).

header.description: The JWS Unprotected Header as a JSON object (JSON serializations only). Unconstrained: header errors are under test.

key.description: The signing JWK (RFC 7517 §4) as a JSON object, imported with the library's JWK import. Unconstrained: an import error is the vector's outcome.

jws_sign_input.description: Sign a payload (RFC 7515 §5.1) in one serialization, with one signer (compact, flattened) or several (general, in order), attached or detached (RFC 7515 Appendix F).

payload_b64u.description: The JWS Payload octets, canonical base64url; the runner decodes them (with b64:false, RFC 7797, the octets themselves are signed).

detached.description: Leave the payload out of the output (RFC 7515 Appendix F).

jws_sign_exact.description: A deterministic signature (HMAC, EdDSA): the exact output. A compact JWS is compared as a string; a JSON JWS is compared as a JSON value, so member order does not matter (RFC 8259 §4) but every octet of every string does.

jws_verify_with.description: The key and allow-list a runner verifies its own randomized output with.

jws_sign_roundtrip.description: A randomized signature (ECDSA): the runner checks that its output has the requested serialization's shape, verifies it with verify_with (passing the payload separately when detached), and checks the verified payload equals payload_b64u. Any failure there fails the vector.

jws_verify_input.description: Verify a JWS (RFC 7515 §5.2) with one key and an allow-list (RFC 8725 §3.1), under the processing order of ADR 0026 §2. The runner imports key, then builds the options, then verifies; the first error is the outcome.

key.description: A JWK (RFC 7517 §4) as a JSON object, imported with the library's JWK import. Unconstrained: an import error is the vector's outcome.

detached_payload_b64u.description: The detached payload (RFC 7515 Appendix F); the JWS then carries none.

max_input_len.description: The largest serialized JWS accepted, in octets (ADR 0026 §7); the library default when absent.

max_signatures.description: The most signatures a general JSON JWS may have (ADR 0026 §7); the library default when absent.

jws_verify_ok.description: The verified JWS: its payload, the alg of the signature that verified, and that signature's index (0 for compact and flattened; the first that verifies, in array order, for general, ADR 0026 §3).

jwe_recipient.description: One recipient to encrypt to (RFC 7516 §5.1 steps 1-8). The runner imports key, then parses header; the first error is the outcome.

alg.description: The JWE "alg" (RFC 7516 §4.1.1), passed as given; an unimplemented one is the library's UnsupportedAlgorithm.

key.description: The recipient's JWK (RFC 7517 §4) as a JSON object: a public key, or the oct key of dir, A*KW, A*GCMKW or the PBES2 password. Unconstrained: an import error is the vector's outcome.

header.description: The JWE Per-Recipient Unprotected Header (RFC 7516 §7.2.1) as a JSON object (JSON serializations only). Unconstrained: header errors are under test.

p2c.description: The PBES2 iteration count (RFC 7518 §4.8.1.2); the library default (10,000, ADR 0023) when absent.

p2s_len.description: The length of the random PBES2 salt input, in octets (RFC 7518 §4.8.1.1); the library default (16) when absent.

jwe_encrypt_input.description: Encrypt a plaintext (RFC 7516 §5.1) in one serialization to one recipient (compact, flattened) or several (general, in order). The runner builds the recipients, then parses protected, then unprotected; the first error is the outcome. With rng_b64u or protected_b64u it calls the library's reproducible encryption (feature insecure-test-vectors, which the vector must list in features).

protected.description: Extra JWE Protected Header parameters (typ, cty, kid, ...) as a JSON object; polyjose sets alg, enc, zip and the key management parameters itself and refuses them here (InvalidHeader).

protected_b64u.description: The exact encoded JWE Protected Header to reproduce (feature insecure-test-vectors): used verbatim for the AAD and the output only if it decodes to a header JSON-equal to the one polyjose builds, else InvalidFormat.

unprotected.description: The JWE Shared Unprotected Header (RFC 7516 §7.2.1) as a JSON object (JSON serializations only).

aad_b64u.description: The JWE AAD octets (RFC 7516 §7.2.1; JSON serializations only).

compress.description: Compress with zip DEF (RFC 7516 §4.1.3; feature deflate, which the vector must list in features).

rng_b64u.description: The octets the encryption draws, in the documented order (CEK, then each recipient's key management, then the content IV; feature insecure-test-vectors). Every octet must be drawn.

jwe_encrypt_exact.description: A reproducible encryption's exact output (rng_b64u given): a compact JWE is compared as a string; a JSON JWE is compared as a JSON value, so member order does not matter (RFC 8259 §4) but every octet of every string does.

jwe_decrypt_with.description: The key and allow-lists a runner decrypts its own randomized output with.

jwe_encrypt_roundtrip.description: A randomized encryption (OS CSPRNG): the runner checks that its output has the requested serialization's shape, decrypts it with decrypt_with, and checks the plaintext equals plaintext_b64u. Any failure there fails the vector.

jwe_decrypt_input.description: Decrypt a JWE (RFC 7516 §5.2) with one key and the allow-lists (RFC 8725 §3.1), under the plan's error order (ADR 0026 §2 applied to JWE). The runner imports key, then builds the policy, then decrypts; the first error is the outcome.

key.description: A JWK (RFC 7517 §4) as a JSON object, imported with the library's JWK import. Unconstrained: an import error is the vector's outcome.

understood_crit.description: The crit extension names the caller understands (RFC 7516 §4.1.13); none when absent.

max_input_len.description: The largest serialized JWE accepted, in octets (ADR 0026 §7); the library default (1 MiB) when absent.

max_recipients.description: The most recipients a JSON JWE may have (ADR 0026 §7); the library default (16) when absent.

max_pbes2_count.description: The largest PBES2 p2c accepted (ADR 0023); the library default (10,000) when absent.

max_decompressed_len.description: The largest inflated plaintext (ADR 0017); the library default (250,000) when absent.

jwe_decrypt_ok.description: The decrypted JWE: its plaintext, and the index of the recipient that decrypted (0 for compact and flattened; the first that decrypts, in array order, for general).
